note: Examples by what they DO. `needs` says what has to be on disk: `starter` runs here with nothing but `npm install`; `gallery` needs scripts/add-gallery.sh, which pulls AGPL sources from the Ranger repository.

examples.title: Hello, and the build loop
examples.does: One class, one print — and the `rgr` loop that fails loudly when the compile fails.

examples.title: Two files, a test, and fourteen targets
examples.does: The project this starter is: an entry point, a class it imports, a test that exits non-zero, and a matrix that compiles the lot to every target Ranger has.
examples.run: npm start && npm test && npm run targets
teaches: a test CI can fail on

examples.title: A parser and evaluator, in three languages
examples.does: Tokenises and evaluates arithmetic with a recursive-descent parser, then runs the SAME source as JavaScript, Python and Go.

examples.title: A PDF with no browser in it
examples.does: Lays a document out with EVG — a CSS engine written in Ranger — and prints it as a real PDF with embedded fonts and vector graphics.

examples.title: Markdown to PDF and to PowerPoint, with diagrams
examples.does: A Markdown document with ```mermaid, ```plantuml, ```dot, ```d2 and ```vega-lite fences, laid out and printed. The diagrams are geometry, not pictures.

examples.title: Diagrams from text
examples.does: Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz and D2 parsed and laid out by RangerFlow — a graph engine with its own routing.

examples.title: Vega charts without Vega
examples.does: Vega and Vega-Lite specifications rendered by Vela, in Ranger, to the same display list EVG prints.

examples.title: An application, not a picture of one
examples.does: A routed, responsive, accessible app written as HTML-shaped markup and checked without a browser.

examples.title: A Figma file, written and read
examples.does: Reads a .fig (Kiwi + zstd) and writes one: frames, text, vector networks, a thumbnail.

examples.title: Reading a codebase
examples.does: Analyses a JavaScript or C++ project and draws its classes, dependencies and sources as a navigable graph.
teaches: a tool that reads a tree

examples.title: A spreadsheet
examples.does: Grid, formulas and XLSX reading and writing.

examples.title: The same screen on iOS and Android
examples.does: One Ranger source driving a Swift host and a Kotlin host — the layout, the state machine and the list are shared; only the window is native.
examples.where: gallery/process_counter_ios, gallery/process_counter_android in the Ranger repository
teaches: a native host around shared logic
